Signed 32.32-style fixed-point number split into 32-bit whole and a decimal fraction scaled to 1e8. Helpers for add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/compare and formatting are declared below.

functions.name: lws_fx_add
functions.signature: const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_add(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b)
functions.description: Adds two 32.32-style fixed-point values (lws_fx_t) and stores the result in r. Typical usage: pass valid a and b; r receives the sum; the function returns r.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to lws_fx_t.
a and b must be valid, non-NULL pointers to initialized lws_fx_t values.
Each lws_fx_t should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 (LWS_FX_FRACTION_MSD) and the sign of frac should match the sign of whole (convention inferred from lws_fx_set).
Overflow or saturation behavior is unknown; callers should avoid inputs whose sum would exceed the representable range.

functions.name: lws_fx_sub
functions.signature: const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_sub(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b)
functions.description: Subtracts fixed-point value b from a and stores the result in r. Returns r.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to lws_fx_t.
a and b must be valid, non-NULL pointers to initialized lws_fx_t values.
Each lws_fx_t should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).
Overflow/underflow behavior is unknown; avoid inputs whose difference would exceed representable range.

functions.description: Multiplies two fixed-point values a and b and stores the result in r. Returns r.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to lws_fx_t.
a and b must be valid, non-NULL pointers to initialized lws_fx_t values.
Each lws_fx_t should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).
Result range/overflow behavior is unknown; choose operands so the product is representable.

functions.name: lws_fx_div
functions.signature: const lws_fx_t * lws_fx_div(lws_fx_t *r, const lws_fx_t *a, const lws_fx_t *b)
functions.description: Divides fixed-point value a by b and stores the result in r. Returns r.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to lws_fx_t.
a and b must be valid, non-NULL pointers to initialized lws_fx_t values.
b must not represent zero; division-by-zero handling is not defined here (requirement inferred from function semantics).
Each lws_fx_t should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).
Quotient range/overflow behavior is unknown; choose operands accordingly.

functions.name: lws_fx_sqrt
functions.description: Computes the square root of fixed-point value a and stores the result in r. Returns r.
requirements: r must be a valid, writable pointer to lws_fx_t.
a must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized lws_fx_t value.
a should represent a non-negative value; behavior for negative inputs is unspecified here (inferred).
Input should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).

functions.name: lws_fx_comp
functions.description: Compares two fixed-point values a and b and returns an int indicating their ordering. Exact return convention (negative/zero/positive vs specific constants) is not documented here; assume a standard comparator pattern (inferred).
requirements: a and b must be valid, non-NULL pointers to initialized lws_fx_t values.
Inputs should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).
Caller must interpret the returned int according to library conventions; exact values are not specified in this header.

functions.name: lws_fx_roundup
functions.description: Rounds the fixed-point value a up to an integer and returns it as int (ceil-like semantics inferred by name).
requirements: a must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized lws_fx_t.
Input should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).
The rounded result must fit in the C int range; behavior on overflow is unspecified.

functions.name: lws_fx_rounddown
functions.description: Rounds the fixed-point value a down to an integer and returns it as int (floor-like semantics inferred by name).
requirements: a must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized lws_fx_t.
Input should be normalized: |frac| < 100000000 and frac sign matches whole (inferred).
The rounded result must fit in the C int range; behavior on overflow is unspecified.

functions.name: lws_fx_string
functions.signature: const char * lws_fx_string(const lws_fx_t *a, char *buf, size_t size)
functions.description: Formats the fixed-point value a into a human-readable string written to buf and returns a pointer to the resulting C string (likely buf). Exact formatting and required buffer size are not specified here.
requirements: a must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized lws_fx_t.
buf must be a valid, non-NULL writable buffer; size must specify its length in bytes.
size should be large enough to hold the full textual representation plus NUL terminator; the exact minimum required size is unknown from this header.
